prompts.text: Which school subject did you enjoy enough to talk about at home?
Tell us about the first time your family celebrated a result you were proud of.
A younger relative feels embarrassed about struggling in one subject. What would help them feel comfortable asking for support?
Teach each other a simple maths trick or swap a favourite writing exercise?
Families often learn how different everyone's thinking is when they attempt the same puzzle.
Showing interest in someone's effort is more useful than asking only about their grades.
What's one thing a sibling or cousin taught you without realising?
Describe a skill you developed through a school club or neighbourhood group.
Someone at home wants a quiet place to study while others have visitors. How should we arrange the space?
Which learning experience brought your family closer together?
Who sends the most entertaining messages in our family chat?
A short phone call after work or a voice note with the full story?
Tell us about a family message you saved because it still makes you smile.
A relative rarely replies to messages but enjoys phone conversations. What would be a considerate way to stay in touch?
People sometimes read silence in a group chat as a sign of distance when it reflects a busy week.
Not every family announcement needs an immediate reply from everyone.
Which topic would make a great weekly question in our family group?
Recall a call with a distant relative that felt much shorter than it was.
A family member is learning to use a new phone. How would you explain group messages without overwhelming them?
Share an old photograph in the family chat or tell everyone the story behind it over a call?
Which creative talent in our family deserves more attention?
Tell us about a homemade gift you received and the effort behind it.
Spend an afternoon drawing together or learn the rhythm of a familiar song?
A younger cousin asks to perform at a family get-together but feels nervous. How would you encourage them?
People sometimes hide their hobbies because they assume their relatives won't understand them.
Showing up for someone's small performance matters even if the style isn't your favourite.
Who has the most unexpected taste in films or music among our relatives?
Describe a time someone's creative project changed your opinion of their ability.
We decide to put together a family playlist with one song from each person. How should we order the songs?
What's a hobby you would like to enjoy with a relative from another generation?
What was the first thing you saved up to buy with your own money?
Compare money-saving habits or exchange tips for avoiding waste at home?
Tell us about a purchase an older relative helped you think through.
A child wants something expensive and doesn't understand the cost. How would you explain the choice without shaming them?
Households often inherit different views about spending from earlier generations.
Teaching budgeting works better with real examples than with warnings alone.
Which family expense deserves more discussion before people commit to contributing?
Recall an occasion when relatives combined their efforts to solve a practical problem.
An extended-family gathering has a limited budget. What should we prioritise before choosing extras?
Share useful second-hand items within the family or organise a seasonal swap?
Who in the neighbourhood was like an extra family member when you were growing up?
Describe a childhood friendship between families that lasted for years.
Host neighbours for a simple afternoon snack or join a local community event?
A new family moves into the building and doesn't know the area. What information would be helpful to share?
Small neighbourhood courtesies often shape how safe and welcome people feel.
Being a good neighbour doesn't require becoming close friends with everyone.
Which neighbour or family friend helped your household during a difficult time?
Tell us about a community celebration where you met someone who became important to the family.
Our street wants volunteers for a shared project. How should family members decide who takes part?
What local custom made your childhood neighbourhood distinctive?
What's one change in family life you handled more easily than you expected?
Mark a move to a new home with a meal together or take a final walk around the old neighbourhood?
Tell us about packing up a room and finding an object you'd forgotten.
A relative relocates for work and wants to stay involved in family decisions. What routine would help?
Moving away sometimes changes the frequency of contact without changing the affection behind it.
Families grow healthier when they allow each member's routine to change over time.
Which part of a new city would you want a relative to show you first?
Describe the first family gathering after someone had been away for a long time.
A family member returns from living overseas and finds old routines unfamiliar. How would you make space for their changes?
Plan a welcome-home breakfast or take a relaxed drive around familiar places?
Which job did you dream of doing when you were much younger?
Tell us about the first time you saw a relative working and understood what their job involved.
Ask an older relative about their first job or ask a younger one about their future plans?
Someone wants to switch careers but worries about disappointing the family. What would be a supportive first response?
Family members sometimes define success differently because they grew up in different circumstances.
A good career conversation starts with curiosity rather than comparisons.
Which practical career lesson have you learnt from a relative's experience?
Recall someone in the family showing patience while you learnt a new task.
A younger family member receives two offers with different benefits. Which questions should we encourage them to ask?
What do you wish your relatives understood better about your daily work?
What's the most thoughtful way someone in our family has welcomed a guest?
Keep a spare place at dinner for visitors or arrange visits in advance?
Tell us about meeting a distant relative for the first time and finding something in common.
An unexpected guest arrives while everyone has separate plans. How would you balance hospitality and everyone's time?
Households have different ideas about which spaces guests should enter and which stay private.
A good host respects the people who live in the home as much as the people who visit.
Which family gathering taught you a new story about someone you thought you knew well?
Describe an unexpected conversation at a family table that changed your mind about someone.
A visitor has dietary needs our usual meals don't meet. What's a considerate way to plan food?
Sit outside for a long conversation with visitors or gather indoors around a simple activity?
When a relative disagrees with you, what helps you feel they are still listening?
Tell us about a misunderstanding that ended with everyone learning something useful.
Discuss a sensitive issue during a quiet walk or arrange a private conversation at home?
Two family members both think the other should apologise first. How might someone help them restart the conversation?
People sometimes use different words to describe the same feeling of disappointment.
A family apology matters more when behaviour changes afterwards.
Which kind of advice sounds helpful to you rather than judgemental?
Recall a time someone gave you room to explain yourself before offering an opinion.
A relative shares news they aren't ready to tell the wider family. How should we respect their choice?
What helps you recognise the right moment to revisit an unfinished family conversation?
What ordinary family experience would you want to preserve in a time capsule?
Collect favourite family recipes in a booklet or put together a map of meaningful places?
Tell us about a keepsake whose importance only became clear when someone explained it.
We decide to preserve family memories digitally but some relatives prefer paper. What approach would suit both?
A family archive tells a richer story when every generation gets a chance to contribute.
Preserving history is worthwhile even when nobody expects to publish the stories.
Which everyday photograph of the family would you choose to display?
Describe a moment when a younger relative asked a question that made you revisit an old memory.
The family chooses one activity to repeat every year without spending much. What would make it easy for everyone to join?
End a reunion by sharing favourite memories or by choosing a small plan for next time?
